assessment_type: Code and historical-evidence based; prospective options are not measured implementations.

options.D: Reduce frequency or defer advisory persistence

criteria.A: No explicit dependency on Python; shared SQLite lock still couples latency.
criteria.B: Collector depends on a coordinator for durable success; do not silently fall back to concurrent direct writes.
criteria.C: Collector keeps its writer and does not await shadow acknowledgments; shared hardware remains.
criteria.D: Collector stays independent, but same-database collision remains on any admitted write.

criteria.A: Measured mixed: latest pairs 4/5, including 30.8624 ms over 25 ms.
criteria.B: Unmeasured; ordering can avoid multiple coordinator writers but adds IPC and queue delay.
criteria.C: Unmeasured; removes advisory write-lock sharing, not read, CPU, disk or checkpoint I/O costs.
criteria.D: Unmeasured frequency changes; fewer attempts may reduce exposure, not bound an individual collision.

criteria.A: Cannot preempt a shadow writer; heartbeat and API writes are not signalled.
criteria.B: Current transaction remains nonpreemptible; all relevant writers must join the protocol.
criteria.C: Separate locks; same-device disk stalls and long source readers can still degrade health commits.
criteria.D: Same nonpreemptible writer; repeated deferral may starve shadow persistence.

criteria.A: One transaction for shadow ledger and checkpoint; failure status is best-effort outside it.
criteria.B: Requires commit acknowledgments, idempotent submissions and coordinator restart handling.
criteria.C: One shadow-ledger transaction, no assumed cross-file commit; generation fence and reconciliation required.
criteria.D: Discard volatile uncommitted work; restart from last durable checkpoint, not a memory cursor.

criteria.A: Existing event digest and conflict tests apply.
criteria.B: Keep event IDs, conflict checks and transactional receipts at the writer.
criteria.C: Keep event digests, receipts and eligibility in the shadow database; no second health-side event ledger.
criteria.D: Re-export committed history; retention may remove evidence before recovery.

criteria.A: Checkpoint and sample existence checked under the same immediate write transaction.
criteria.B: Keep these checks inside the coordinator transaction, not before queueing.
criteria.C: Local shadow checkpoint CAS remains atomic, but current same-database sample checks must be redesigned.
criteria.D: Advance only with the whole successful consume transaction; never pre-acknowledge deferred writes.

criteria.A: Controlled replay is tested; live duplicate-notice blocker remains.
criteria.B: Retries need idempotent commit receipts; queue delivery is not exactly once.
criteria.C: Preserve IDs on migration, fence dataset resets and mismatched restores; unknown provenance is ineligible.
criteria.D: Replay and rebase guards remain necessary after outages or delayed writes.

criteria.A: None for retention of current design.
criteria.B: High: inventory and route collector, heartbeat, API, maintenance and shadow writes.
criteria.C: Moderate to high: split connections, provenance fence, idempotent import, read and clear compatibility.
criteria.D: Lower code footprint but changes freshness and recovery semantics; separate approval still required.

criteria.A: New activity word; durable checkpoint survives; stale worker lock rules unchanged.
criteria.B: Coordinator availability and queue receipts must recover before acknowledging writes.
criteria.C: Validate dataset generation, schema and last receipt; health collection does not wait for shadow startup.
criteria.D: Bounded recomputation from history; expired anchors need conservative bootstrap.

criteria.A: Existing authenticated loopback export and read-only dashboard.
criteria.B: IPC authorization, bounded typed operations and secret-safe failure paths are new surfaces.
criteria.C: Fixed local paths, source read-only connection, second file and WAL sidecars in retention/backup/deletion scope.
criteria.D: Bounded memory must not retain raw telemetry or tokens in logs; existing transport stays unchanged.

criteria.A: Lowest; track stalls and freshness, keep activation blocked.
criteria.B: Highest: central availability, queue admission, control-plane calls and drain semantics.
criteria.C: Two database lifecycles but no mandatory shared writer broker.
criteria.D: Small implementation, complex starvation and freshness interpretation.

criteria.A: Simple but recurring shared-writer failures remain.
criteria.B: Strong writer ownership only if every caller is covered; intrusive for a local assistant.
criteria.C: Clear authoritative/advisory ownership fits failure isolation, contingent on explicit cross-store lifecycle.
criteria.D: Useful complementary budget policy, not a replacement for isolation.

recommendation: C is preferred for a separately approved prototype and validation phase, not immediate activation. Keep A unchanged until then; use bounded D-style throttling only as a future complement.
